chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

If a Muslim man apostatizes from Islam, his wife becomes separated from him just as a woman becomes separated after a third divorce, and she observes the waiting period from him as a divorced woman observes it. If he returns to Islam and repents before she marries, then he is only a suitor, and there is no waiting period upon her for him; rather, the waiting period upon her is only for another man. If he is killed or dies before the completion of the waiting period, she observes from him the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died; thus she inherits from him during the waiting period, but he does not inherit from her if she dies while he is an apostate from Islam.

key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةُ ثَلَاثاً: a woman irrevocably separated after three divorces
key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife became legally separated from him
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: the waiting period of a widow
key_terms.مُرْتَدٌّ عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ: one who is apostate from Islam

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shia fiqh to a marriage and inheritance rights when a Muslim husband apostasizes from Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the marriage and inheritance consequences of a Muslim man who apostasizes from Islam. It explains the woman's separation, her 'iddah, the effect of his repentance before her remarriage, and the inheritance rule if he dies during her waiting period while still denying inheritance to the apostate husband from her estate.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5713 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami from Abu Abdullah (as) who said: "If a Muslim man apostatizes from Islam, his wife becomes separated from him just as a woman becomes separated after a third divorce, and she must observe the waiting period (iddah) as a divorced woman does.

If he returns to Islam and repents before she marries another man, he may propose to her again, and she is not required to observe any waiting period for him, though she must observe it for anyone else.
However, if he is killed or dies before the completion of her waiting period, she must observe the waiting period of a widow (iddah of a deceased husband), and during that period, she inherits from him. But if she dies while he is still an apostate, he does not inherit from her."
